title: Поклонница господина Огузка  (An Admirer for Mister Oguzok)

segments.t: As the staff members grumble about sharing facilities, Kostya comes into the kitchen to tell Max that his regular older lady has arrived in the dining room again. To the amusement of the other cooks, the guest asks specifically for Max to prepare her meal.
Фу, я после него туда не пойду.
А добрый день, добрый день, дорогие друзья.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Фу, я после него туда не пойду.
'Ugh, I am not going in there after him.' The meaning hinges on 'ugh' working together with 'go' in spoken Russian.
'Good afternoon to you.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'good' and finishing on 'days'.
'I was simply eating.' Max brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'just' in a few short words. Kostya answers right away.
'You should have done it the other way around.' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'contrary' in spoken Russian.
'There is a time for everything.' Notice how Russian expresses 'whole' and 'time' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Your retired lady friend just arrived out there.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'there' and finishing on 'came'. Max answers right away.
А добрый день, добрый день, дорогие друзья.
'Ah, good afternoon, good afternoon, dear friends.' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'friends' without extra filler words.
'Who are you filming right now?' Kostya raises the pitch on 'are taking off' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'The thing is.' The grammar packs 'matter' and 'that' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Kostya answers right away.
'Film me instead.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'me' and finishing on 'take off'.
'Mister Oguzok.' Max brings out the contrast between 'Mr' and 'rookie' in a few short words.
'Why does she only want you to cook?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'what' before landing on 'you'. Max answers right away.
'You guys are simply jealous of me.' The grammar packs 'just' and 'to envy' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Фу, я после него туда не пойду.
А добрый день, добрый день, дорогие друзья.
When you watch Scene 3 of Episode 19, listen out for the exchange around an admirer for mister oguzok — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
